paragraphs.heading: What a semi-arid climate is
paragraphs.text: A semi-arid climate, also called a semi-desert or steppe climate, is one kind of dry climate. Places with it receive less precipitation than their potential evapotranspiration, but not as little as a desert does. It comes in several kinds, depending on things like temperature, and each kind gives rise to different biomes.

paragraphs.heading: Drawing the lines
paragraphs.text: A place counts as semi-arid, written BS, when its yearly precipitation in millimetres falls below a set threshold but stays above half of it. A mean annual temperature of 18 °C then divides the group. Places warmer than that on average are hot semi-arid (BSh), and the rest are cold semi-arid (BSk).

paragraphs.heading: Hot semi-arid
paragraphs.text: Hot semi-arid climates lie from the high tens to the mid-30s of latitude in the tropics and subtropics, often near tropical savanna or humid subtropical regions. They are most common around the edges of subtropical deserts. Summers are hot, sometimes extremely so, winters are warm to cool, and rain is scarce. Their main homes are Africa, Australia, the Indian subcontinent and the edges of the Iranian plateau; in Australia, much of the Outback around the central desert falls in this group. India and parts of Pakistan get short, clear wet seasons from the monsoons, but not enough rain overall to count as savanna or humid subtropical.

paragraphs.heading: Cold semi-arid
paragraphs.text: Cold semi-arid climates sit in raised parts of the temperate zones, generally from the mid-30s to the low 50s of latitude. They often border humid continental or Mediterranean climates and usually lie inland, some way from large bodies of water. Summers are warm to hot and dry, though not quite as hot as in the hot type. Winters are cold and can freeze, with some snow, but far less than wetter places at the same latitude.

paragraphs.heading: Big swings between day and night
paragraphs.text: Cold semi-arid areas tend to sit higher up, and their temperature can swing by 20 °C or more between day and night. Daily swings that large are rarely seen in hot semi-arid places. The timing of rain also shifts with latitude. Further from the equator, winters are dry and summers wetter; closer to it, the pattern is more like a Mediterranean climate, with dry summers, fairly wet winters, and even wetter springs and autumns.

paragraphs.heading: Where to find them
paragraphs.text: Cold semi-arid climates are most common in central Asia, the western United States and the Middle East, along with other parts of Asia. They also turn up in Northern Africa, South Africa, parts of South America, inland southern Australia around Mildura, and across a large part of Spain and much of southern Ukraine. In Europe, the hot type is found mainly in southeastern Spain.
